Two-stage bootstrap for propagating uncertainty from LME predictions

Source: R/bootstrap_landmark.R
bootstrap_landmark.Rd

bootstrap_landmark() bootstraps the complete landmark workflow. In each replicate, the risk set at every landmark is resampled with replacement, the user's pipeline is re-run on the resampled data (refitting any longitudinal mixed-effects models, regenerating their predictions at each landmark and refitting the landmark survival models), and the coefficients are collected.

The bootstrap distribution quantifies uncertainty from estimating the longitudinal trajectories and its propagation into the landmark survival models, which the standard errors from fit_landmark() ignore. Results are reported as percentile confidence intervals, percentile bootstrap p-values and the median of the bootstrap distribution, next to the full-data fit.

Usage

bootstrap_landmark(
  baseline,
  pipeline,
  n_boot = 200,
  exponentiate = FALSE,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  progress = getOption("tidylandmark.progress", interactive())
)

Arguments

baseline

A landmark_tbl, as returned by landmark_data().

pipeline

A function of one argument, a landmark_tbl, that runs the rest of the workflow (e.g. add_landmark_covariates() then fit_landmark()) and returns a landmark_fit.

n_boot

Number of bootstrap replicates. Default 200.

exponentiate

If TRUE, report hazard ratios (subdistribution hazard ratios for Fine-Gray models) instead of log hazard ratios.

conf.level

Confidence level for the intervals. Default 0.95.

alternative

Alternative hypothesis for the bootstrap p-values: one of "two.sided" (default), "greater" or "less".

progress

Show a progress bar over replicates? Defaults to the tidylandmark.progress option, or interactive() if it is unset.

Value

A tibble with one row per landmark and term of the full-data fit:

  • .landmark, .model, .cause, origin, term: as in tidy.landmark_fit().

  • estimate__full, conf.low__full, conf.high__full, p.value__full: the full-data fit with model-based (Wald) inference.

  • estimate__boot, conf.low__boot, conf.high__boot, p.value__boot: median, percentile interval and percentile p-value of the bootstrap distribution.

  • n_boot_ok: replicates with an estimate for this term.

  • .fit_status__full, .message__full: fit status of the full-data fit.

  • .estimates__boot: one estimate per replicate, in draw order.

  • .fit_status__boot, .message__boot: list-columns with the fit status and message for the same replicate, landmark and term.

Details

Resampling

Rows are resampled independently within each landmark, which matches fit_landmark() fitting one independent model per landmark and add_landmark_covariates() fitting one mixed model per landmark from that landmark's risk set. The bootstrap therefore supports per-landmark inference, but not comparisons between landmarks. A subject drawn more than once is treated as distinct subjects, each with its own random effects in the mixed models.

Risk sets are read from the rows of baseline as they are now, so a landmark_tbl filtered after landmark_data() is resampled as filtered. Create any LME predictors used by the survival model inside pipeline so their mixed models are refitted on each draw. For spline coefficients, set the interior and boundary knots before resampling and pass them to the spline function. The bootstrap checks the fitted basis at each landmark.

Failed replicates

Each replicate runs quietly: progress bars (when pipeline uses the default progress), messages and warnings are suppressed, and a replicate whose pipeline errors is recorded as "failed" at every landmark instead of stopping the bootstrap. n_boot_ok gives the number of replicates with an estimate for each term; summaries use only those. Check .fit_status__boot when n_boot_ok is well below n_boot. An unavailable coefficient (for example, a comparison to an absent factor level) has an NA estimate in that draw. Intervals and p-values require at least two usable estimates.

Reproducibility and p-values

Results depend on the random number generator; call set.seed() first for reproducible results. A zero p-value means that no usable draw fell in the relevant tail. Its Monte Carlo precision depends on n_boot_ok.

See also

landmark_data(), add_landmark_covariates(), fit_landmark(), tidy.landmark_fit()

Examples

# \donttest{
# PBC: status 0 = censored, 1 = transplant, 2 = death
set.seed(2026)
pbcseq_baseline |>
  landmark_data(id, futime, status, landmarks = c(365, 730), horizon = 1825) |>
  bootstrap_landmark(
    pipeline = \(data) {
      data |>
        add_landmark_covariates(pbcseq_visits, id, day, lme = c(bili, albumin)) |>
        fit_landmark(~ age + log(bili) + albumin, cause = 2)
    },
    n_boot = 50
  )
